name: Receive, test and report clinical trial visit samples in the central laboratory
sector: medical laboratory services (clinical trial central laboratory)
summary: Investigator sites collect blood and urine from trial participants at each study visit using the company's pre-labelled kits and ship them overnight to the central laboratory. Sample management technicians check the samples against the requisition and the protocol, process and aliquot them, and core laboratory technologists run the safety tests, with specialty tests run in later batches. Results that hit protocol alert values are phoned to the investigator, a data coordinator reviews each visit against the study's enrolment and visit schedule before the report goes to the site, and discrepancies become queries that can take days to resolve. Unusable samples, batched specialty tests and slow site replies to queries are the main sources of delay.

baseline.org_archetype: The clinical trials central laboratory line of a large Canadian laboratory company, serving 30 to 60 active Phase I to IV studies with testing in the shared core laboratory.
baseline.notes: Starts when a courier box from a site arrives and ends when the visit report is released to the site and the study database (or reissued after a query), or the sample set is unusable. Kit building, sample storage and monthly sponsor data transfers are separate processes.

trigger: A courier shipment with one participant's visit samples and requisition arrives from an investigator site.
end_state: The visit's results are reported to the site and posted to the study database, with any query closed and a corrected report issued, and retention aliquots passed to storage; or the set is rejected and recollection requested.

volume.seasonality: Follows enrolment in active studies; dips over holidays when sites see fewer participants; Monday and Tuesday arrivals are heaviest as weekend visits are rare.

evidence.note: Phase I to IV central lab service (dyn_cts); volume follows the organisation file's estimate of 30 to 60 active studies.

roles.title: Kit production and sample management technician
roles.department: Trial kit, sample and data operations

evidence.note: Sample receipt, accessioning and protocol processing by trial sample management technicians; FTE is 5,000 visit sample sets a month at about 15 minutes each. The organisation file's 14 technicians also build about 5,000 kits a month and run storage, which looks tight. Loaded cost from the organisation file (Job Bank 33101 wage times 1.35).

roles.title: Medical laboratory technologist, chemistry and haematology

evidence.note: Core laboratory technologists test trial samples alongside other work (organisation file assumption); about 12 minutes per visit set including specialty tests and film reviews. Loaded cost from the organisation file (Job Bank 32120 wage times 1.35).

roles.title: Clinical data coordinator
roles.department: Trial kit, sample and data operations

evidence.note: Data review, query handling and corrected reports; about 8 minutes per visit set on average. The rest of the 8 coordinators' time is monthly data transfers. Loaded cost from the organisation file.

Project teams answer urgent site questions within hours (dyn_cts) and alert values must be notified immediately (ezzelle2008); about 5 per cent of visit sets at about 24 minutes including the sponsor notice. Loaded cost from the organisation file.

systems.name: Clinical trial central lab system (study build, kit inventory, sample tracking, data transfer)
Laboratory information system (orders, accessioning, results, autoverification rules)
Automated chemistry and immunoassay analysers on track lines
Haematology analysers, slide makers and coagulation analysers
Quality control data management software (rules, peer comparison)
Study-specific paper requisition shipped with the visit kit
Centrifuges, aliquoting stations and temporary sample freezers

steps.name: Receive the courier shipment and check its condition
steps.description: A sample management technician signs for the overnight courier boxes from investigator sites, checks that ambient, refrigerated and dry-ice shippers are intact and at the right temperature, scans the waybill and logs the arrival time in the trial system. Most shipments arrive in the morning courier wave.

error.defect_description: Temperature condition not recorded on arrival.

control.basis: Sample receipt and dangerous goods shipping checks under GCLP (audit trail from collection to disposal)

evidence.note: Tracked shipments with TDG and IATA trained staff (dyn_cts); receipt audit trail (ezzelle2008). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Accession the visit samples against the requisition
steps.description: The technician opens the kit, scans the pre-printed kit barcode, checks each tube label against the requisition (subject number, visit, collection date and time) and against the tubes the protocol expects for that visit, checks stability time, volume and haemolysis, and confirms the accession so orders are created in the trial system and the LIS.

error.defect_description: Requisition field keyed wrongly or a missing tube not recorded.

control.basis: GCLP specimen acceptance and rejection criteria and the study laboratory manual

next.condition: tube unacceptable (outside stability, wrong temperature, broken, insufficient) or unidentifiable

evidence.note: Label and requisition checks and acceptance criteria from ezzelle2008; protocol stability requirements from iqvia_cl. Rejection share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Notify the site of an unacceptable or unidentifiable sample
steps.description: The data coordinator records the problem in the trial system, cancels the affected tests, and emails or faxes the site coordinator with the reason so the site can recollect at an unscheduled visit or confirm the subject's identity. Remaining acceptable tubes go on to testing.

error.defect_description: Notification sent without the full reason, causing a follow-up call.

control.basis: Study laboratory manual and sponsor contract: sample rejection notified to the site and sponsor

next.condition: other tubes in the set can be tested

evidence.note: Discrepancy resolution before processing (ezzelle2008); shares are estimates.

steps.name: Process and aliquot the samples per the laboratory manual
steps.description: The technician centrifuges the tubes as the protocol requires, pours testing aliquots and retention aliquots into pre-labelled tubes and cryovials, scans each aliquot to the sample record, and freezes aliquots that will be stored or batch-tested later.

error.defect_description: Aliquot labelled with the wrong visit.

control.basis: Sponsor protocol and study laboratory manual processing instructions

evidence.note: Storage and transfer per protocol (dyn_cts) and sample lifecycle tracking (iqvia_cl, acm_global); times are estimates.

steps.name: Transfer the testing aliquots to the core laboratory
steps.description: The technician scans the aliquots onto a transfer list and carries the rack to the core laboratory's chemistry and haematology area, where a technologist scans receipt.

error.defect_description: Aliquot left off the transfer list.

evidence.note: Internal tracking of transfers is standard GCLP audit trail practice; times are estimates.

steps.name: Load the trial samples on the analysers
steps.description: A core laboratory technologist loads the trial aliquots on the chemistry, immunoassay and haematology analysers between community lab runs, using the study's test codes and units.

error.defect_description: Sample loaded under the wrong test code.

evidence.note: Organisation file assumes trial testing runs in the shared core laboratory; times are estimates.

steps.name: Run the safety tests on the analysers
steps.description: The analysers run the panel (chemistry, haematology, urinalysis) with the run's quality control and send results to the LIS through the middleware.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Analyser run times are estimates.

steps.name: Review and verify the results
steps.description: The technologist checks the run's QC is acceptable, reviews instrument flags, delta and linearity limits, repeats or dilutes results where needed and verifies them in the LIS. Results for the study are not autoverified.

error.defect_description: Result verified despite a flag that needed a repeat.

control.basis: QC acceptable before reporting (GCLP; ISO 15189 and CAP accreditation)

next.condition: all tests for the visit complete
haematology flag needs a blood film review

evidence.note: QC before reporting from ezzelle2008; GCLP fills the gap between GCP and GLP for trial sample analysis (wiki_gclp). Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Review a blood film for the flagged haematology result
steps.description: For a count flagged by the analyser (abnormal cells, platelet clumps), the technologist makes and stains a slide, reviews it under the microscope or on the digital imaging system, records the differential or morphology comment and verifies the result.

error.defect_description: Morphology comment missed.

control.basis: Laboratory review criteria for flagged haematology results (ISO 15189 and CAP accreditation; GCLP)

evidence.note: Standard haematology practice; share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Run the specialty or batched esoteric tests
steps.description: Tests outside the safety panel (coagulation, special chemistry, biomarkers run in weekly batches, or tests sent to the specialty laboratory) are run when their batch is scheduled, and the results are verified and added to the visit record.

error.defect_description: Batch result attached to the wrong visit.

control.basis: Method validation and QC for specialty assays (GCLP)

evidence.note: Esoteric tests offered (dyn_cts) and validation of non-standard assays (ezzelle2008); batch frequency is an estimate.

steps.name: Check results against the protocol alert ranges
steps.description: The trial system compares each verified result with the study's reference ranges and the protocol's alert and exclusion values and flags any result that must be phoned to the investigator.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Alert values defined with study clinicians (ezzelle2008); alert share is an estimate.

steps.name: Phone the alert result to the investigator site
steps.description: A project team member calls the site coordinator or investigator, reads back the result, records who was reached and when in the trial system, and retries or escalates to the sponsor's medical monitor when nobody answers. After hours the on-call team makes the call.

error.defect_description: Call not documented or made late.

control.basis: Protocol alert values and GCLP immediate notification of alert results

evidence.note: Immediate notification (ezzelle2008); urgent responses within hours including after hours (dyn_cts). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Notify the sponsor's medical monitor of the alert
steps.description: Where the protocol asks for it, the project team member emails the alert result and the time the site was told to the sponsor's or CRO's medical monitor, and files the notification in the study records.

error.defect_description: Notice not sent or not filed.

control.basis: Protocol and sponsor contract alert notification requirements

evidence.note: Project team communication described in dyn_cts; whether and how sponsors are told is protocol specific, so this is an estimate.

steps.name: Review the visit data before release
steps.description: The data coordinator reviews the visit record in the trial system: subject number, initials and birth date against the study's enrolment list, visit name against the visit schedule, collection time, expected tests done or cancelled, and units and ranges, using the system's edit checks.

error.defect_description: Discrepancy missed and passed to the sponsor transfer.

control.basis: Complete and accurate trial records: Good clinical practice for laboratories analysing trial samples (ICH E6; Health Canada Food and Drug Regulations C.05.010 and C.05.012 for Canadian trials)

evidence.note: Accuracy requirement in hc_c05012 and quality systems in hc_c05010; GCP applies to laboratories analysing trial samples (mhra_gcp, ema_e6); data cleaning as a central lab service (labconnect). Results tested in the afternoon are usually reviewed the next morning. Query share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Release the report to the site and the study database
steps.description: The trial system publishes the report to the site portal or fax with study ranges and flags, masking any results the protocol keeps blinded from sites, and posts the results to the study database for the next sponsor data transfer.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Reporting to authorised persons only: Good clinical practice for laboratories analysing trial samples (ICH E6; Health Canada Food and Drug Regulations C.05.010 and C.05.012 for Canadian trials)

evidence.note: Report contents and authorised recipients (ezzelle2008); blinded data management (labconnect); lab-to-sponsor data model (cdisc_lab).

steps.name: Raise a query with the site
steps.description: The coordinator logs the discrepancy (wrong subject number, visit outside window, missing collection time, test missing from the kit) in the query log and sends it to the site coordinator by portal, email or fax with a reply deadline.

error.defect_description: Query worded unclearly, causing a second round.

control.basis: GCLP discrepancy resolution with an audit trail

evidence.note: Discrepancy resolution in ezzelle2008; times are estimates.

steps.name: Release the report with the query flagged
steps.description: So the investigator has the safety results without waiting, the trial system releases the report to the site marked as pending a query, and holds the affected fields out of the sponsor transfer.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Common central laboratory practice; estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the site's answer to the query
steps.description: The site coordinator checks the source documents and replies, often only after the next monitoring visit or once the coordinator has time between patient visits.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Site response times are estimates.

steps.name: Correct the record and reissue the report
steps.description: The coordinator applies the site's answer in the trial system with an audit trail, reissues a corrected report marked as such while keeping the original, and closes the query so the data enter the next transfer.

error.defect_description: Correction applied to the wrong visit.

control.basis: Corrections keep the original and corrected report with an audit trail (GCLP; C.05.012 complete and accurate records)

evidence.note: Correction rules from ezzelle2008; times are estimates.

steps.name: Chase the unanswered query
steps.description: The coordinator re-sends the query, phones the site, and after a second miss lists it on the open-query report the project manager sends to the sponsor's monitor.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Estimate.

exceptions.name: Unacceptable or unidentifiable sample
exceptions.description: Outside stability, wrong temperature, broken, insufficient or unlabelled; the site is told and asked to recollect, and the whole set is lost in about a third of these.

exceptions.name: Protocol alert value
exceptions.description: A result at a protocol alert value is phoned to the investigator and documented.

exceptions.name: Data discrepancy query
exceptions.description: Wrong subject number, visit or collection time; the report goes out flagged and the record is corrected after the site replies, sometimes after reminders.

exceptions.name: Specialty or batched tests
exceptions.description: Tests run in weekly or scheduled batches delay the complete visit report by days.

exceptions.name: Blood film review
exceptions.description: An analyser flag on the blood count needs a slide review before verification.

exceptions.name: Repeat or dilution
exceptions.description: Flags or out-of-range results need a rerun before verification.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from receipt at the laboratory to the visit report released (or corrected)

evidence.note: Central labs commit to each protocol's turnaround (iqvia_cl) without publishing figures; estimate of next-day safety results with batched specialty tests and queries in the tail.

benchmarks.unit: hours, suggested retrieval time for archived records
normal specimens typically used to verify a manufacturer's reference range

benchmarks.value: every six months in the first year, then annually

pain_points.description: Paper requisitions filled in at busy sites carry wrong subject numbers, visits or collection times, and each becomes a query that depends on the site answering.

evidence.note: Query share and site response times are estimates.

pain_points.description: Samples arriving outside stability or at the wrong temperature after courier delays are lost and the participant has to come back.

evidence.note: Rejection share is an estimate.

pain_points.description: Specialty tests run in scheduled batches hold the complete visit report for days.

evidence.note: Batch frequency is an estimate.

pain_points.description: Trial samples share core laboratory analysers and technologists with community testing, so trial runs wait between community runs.

evidence.note: Organisation file assumption that trials testing uses the core laboratory.

pain_points.description: Open queries are tracked partly in spreadsheets and chased by phone and email.

evidence.note: Spreadsheets are listed as a clinical trials system in the organisation file; practice is an estimate.

sources.title: Clinical trial services
sources.supports: Central laboratory testing for Phase I to IV trials with routine safety and esoteric tests; a dedicated project team per study; urgent questions answered within hours including after hours; protocol review; data in multiple electronic formats; TDG and IATA trained staff with tracked shipments; sample storage and transfer per protocol.

sources.title: Guidelines on good clinical laboratory practice: bridging operations between research and clinical research laboratories (Ezzelle et al.)
sources.publisher: Journal of Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Analysis, via PubMed Central
sources.supports: GCLP: each specimen needs a request form with participant ID, collection date and time and collector; labels checked against the form and discrepancies resolved; documented acceptance and rejection criteria; audit trail from collection to disposal; QC acceptable before reporting; alert values defined with study clinicians and notified immediately; reports with receipt time, units and reference ranges; corrections keep original and corrected reports; records retrievable within about 24 hours.

sources.title: Food and Drug Regulations C.05.010 Sponsor's obligations (good clinical practices)
sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: Sponsors must conduct trials under good clinical practices, including systems and procedures that assure the quality of every aspect of the trial, and meet the record requirements of C.05.012.

sources.title: Food and Drug Regulations C.05.012 Records
sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: Trial information must be recorded, handled and stored to allow complete and accurate reporting; records kept for 15 years.

sources.title: ICH E6 Good clinical practice: scientific guideline
sources.supports: ICH E6 sets an international standard for the design, conduct, recording and reporting of clinical trials and defines sponsor and investigator responsibilities; R3 adds a risk-based, proportionate approach (effective July 2025).

sources.title: Good clinical practice for clinical trials
sources.publisher: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency, GOV.UK
sources.supports: Laboratories analysing samples from a clinical trial must comply with GCP; inspections are risk based and findings are graded critical, major or other; subcontracted organisations must give access to records.

sources.title: LAB (laboratory data exchange model)
sources.supports: A standard model for the acquisition and exchange of laboratory data between labs and sponsors or CROs (LAB v1.0.1, 2004).

sources.title: Central laboratories
sources.supports: Central lab services include specimen collection kits, a courier network, a biorepository, project management and data management; labs meet each protocol's turnaround and stability requirements; integrated LIMS and sample lifecycle tracking.

sources.title: LabConnect central laboratory services
sources.supports: Lists custom collection kits, kit tracking, data alignment and cleaning, customised data delivery, blinded data management and biospecimen operations as central lab services.

sources.title: ACM Global Laboratories
sources.supports: Lists clinical trial testing, routine safety testing, customised sample collection kits and advanced sample tracking services for trials in more than 65 countries.

sources.title: Good Clinical Laboratory Practice
sources.supports: GCP does not define laboratory requirements and GLP covers preclinical work, so the Research Quality Association proposed GCLP in 2003; WHO and MHRA later issued GCLP guidance.

sources.title: Wages: Medical technologist, medical laboratory in Ontario (NOC 32120)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low 23.00, median 42.00, high 50.00 CAD (2023-2024).

sources.title: Wages: Medical laboratory technical assistant in Ontario (NOC 33101)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low 17.95, median 26.25, high 36.00 CAD (2023-2024).

assumptions: Testing is done in the shared core laboratory by its technologists, as the organisation file assumes; sample receipt, processing and data review are done by the trials operations team.
The LIS change from the LIS change process is the study build that must be in place before any sample can be tested; it is listed with share 0 because it does not start individual cases.
Discrepancy queries are found when the coordinator reviews the visit record; in practice many are spotted at accessioning and sent the same day, which changes timing only slightly.
Shares of unacceptable samples (4.5 per cent), alert values (5 per cent), queries (12 per cent) and specialty tests (25 per cent) are estimates; no opened source gave rates.

The organisation file's 14 kit production and sample management technicians must also build about 5,000 kits a month and run storage; the 9.8 FTE stated here leaves little for that work, so either headcount or volume in the organisation file may be off.

Health Canada's Food and Drug Regulations Division 5 apply to Canadian trials; trials for foreign sponsors follow ICH E6 and the sponsor's regulator. Controls are marked needs_policy_change because the specific checks are set by protocols and laboratory procedures, though GCP itself is required by law.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage times 1.35).
